theme: Heating pottery that cracks if you rush
title: Kiln Firing Policy: Gate the Ramp by the Thickest Piece
isolation: candidate runs as an isolated stdin->stdout subprocess via isorun; the evaluator's naive-baseline and near-optimal-ceiling references are computed only in the parent process
strategies: flat non-adaptive rate (e.g. 65% of max_rate) for the whole firing: safe-ish but pays the slowdown everywhere, wasting fuel

constant max-rate the whole way (the obvious 'heat as fast as the burner allows' recipe): minimal fuel time, but cracks the thickest piece in mixed-thickness loads at the quartz/cristobalite inversion bands

regime-decomposed schedule: max rate outside the two phase-transition bands, and inside each band an exact-bisection safe rate driven ONLY by the load's thickest piece's analytic thermal-lag ODE, carrying its real cumulative stress across bands in order -- fast where it's free, gated only where and only because the thickest section demands it
the same regime decomposition solved with a tighter (near-optimal) safety margin, closer to the crack threshold, buying back more fuel
